data.narrative:
Terrestrial Energy operates in the nuclear energy sector at the public-company stage, having raised $280M to date. The comparable universe consists of 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 6 private competitors including Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and Fuse Energy. However, the nuclear energy sector presents a constrained peer set for valuation purposes.

The peer-median triangulation method is not applicable here. The nuclear energy sector contains only 5 same-sector peers total, and applying stage, timing, and valuation-tier filters yields insufficient datapoints—only 1 same-stage comparable and 0 adjacent-stage or similar-tier matches. The threshold for reliable peer-median analysis requires a minimum of 3 filtered comparables; this dataset falls short. An all-sector median approach would introduce excessive dispersion and would not reflect nuclear-specific dynamics in capital intensity, regulatory timelines, and technology maturity.

Without sufficient filtered comparables, traditional triangulation cannot be completed with analytical rigor. Any valuation range derived here would depend on alternative methods not present in the provided data—such as DCF modeling with sector-specific assumptions, precedent transaction analysis, or qualitative factor weighting. The primary constraint is data scarcity in the narrow peer set rather than methodological availability. Further valuation work would require either expansion to adjacent subsectors (energy infrastructure, advanced materials) or reliance on non-market approaches.
